evals.prompt: Add a small in-memory cache with TTL in front of a read-heavy lookup function, including an explicit invalidation path when the underlying data changes.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md that treats invalidation as a first-class concern (not just the read-through cache) and pins the TTL + cache size as configurable.
expectations: The Steps section covers cache invalidation/eviction, not only the read-through path.
The Risks section addresses stale reads and the cache-stampede / cold-start case.
The TTL and cache bound are presented as configurable rather than hardcoded.
The body contains the 11 numbered spec sections and a verifiable Done Condition.

evals.prompt: Add structured logging to a service module that currently uses scattered print/console statements, with consistent fields and levels.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md that defines the structured field set and levels and scopes the replacement of existing ad-hoc logging without changing behaviour.
expectations: The plan defines a consistent structured field set and log levels rather than leaving them unspecified.
Scope — Excluded clarifies that behaviour (not just logging) is unchanged — this is not a refactor of business logic.
The Steps section accounts for replacing the existing scattered statements, not only adding new ones.
The body contains the 11 numbered spec sections.

evals.prompt: Gate a new code path behind a feature flag so it is off by default and can be enabled per environment, with a clean removal plan once it ships.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md that specifies the default-off behaviour, the per-environment enablement mechanism, and a flag-removal/cleanup step.
expectations: The Assumptions or Steps section states the flag defaults to off and how it is enabled per environment.
The plan includes a flag-removal / cleanup step for after the path is fully shipped.
The Risks section addresses the dual-path window where both the old and new behaviour can be live.
The body contains the 11 numbered spec sections and a verifiable Done Condition.
